memory_update.text: CAMT should be carried forward as a high-relevance underfollowed HBM inspection/metrology candidate because company-disclosed orders directly mention a leading HBM manufacturer and AI-related OSAT demand.
FORM should be tracked as a probe-card/test-intensity beneficiary of HBM and advanced packaging; next layer should verify actual HBM revenue contribution and customer mix.
ONTO should be tracked as a process-control/metrology/yield-management candidate tied to HBM expansion through Dragonfly 2D inspection and 3D bump metrology.
For this node, US-listed public-market exposure appears stronger in inspection, metrology, and wafer-test/probe cards than in die-thinning, bonding, underfill, and TSV-specific pure plays.

Need a follow-up global ADR/foreign-ordinary pass for Japanese, Korean, Taiwanese, and European suppliers in die thinning, bonding, gap fill, TSV, temporary bonding/debonding, and underfill materials because many direct chokepoint suppliers are not US-listed common stocks.

KLIC should be retained for Layer 2 because it has direct official evidence of first HBM system shipment and fluxless thermocompression bonding exposure, but the key gating issue is how material HBM/TCB revenue is versus legacy bonding equipment.

FORM should be retained for Layer 2 as a HBM wafer/die test and known-good-die yield-management candidate; verify HBM revenue mix and whether demand is tied to recurring probe-card consumables or cyclical capacity additions.

CAMT should be retained for Layer 2 as an advanced packaging inspection/metrology candidate with explicit HBM-manufacturer order signal; verify customer concentration and HBM-specific backlog conversion.

For this node, the most relevant US-listed chokepoint mappings are bonding equipment, HBM wafer/die test, advanced packaging inspection/metrology, and TSV/RDL process control rather than memory producers themselves.

Layer 1B did not fully cover US-listed ADR/foreign ordinary names for Japanese/Taiwanese materials and substrate inputs such as underfill, bonding materials, CMP consumables, ABF film, and copper surface chemistry; those likely require a separate global/non-US-listed pass.

ONTO should remain on the HBM stack-flow watch list as an inspection/metrology candidate because company disclosure identifies a large HBM-manufacturer purchase agreement for Dragonfly 2D inspection and 3D bump metrology through 2027.
FORM should remain on the underfollowed discovery lane as a probe-card / test-gate supplier to memory manufacturers, with explicit HBM demand language in its annual-report disclosure.

KLIC is a lower-attention advanced-packaging equipment candidate; its inclusion depends on verifying whether first HBM system shipment becomes repeat volume demand rather than an isolated evaluation milestone.

For this node, separate direct HBM stack-flow suppliers from broader accelerator substrate/package suppliers; stack-flow suppliers have cleaner exposure to HBM die volume, while substrate suppliers are broader AI accelerator packaging plays.

US-listed underfollowed HBM stack-flow exposure appears concentrated in testing, inspection/metrology, and bonding equipment rather than in pure-play HBM materials; later layers should search for ADRs or foreign ordinary shares if the universe needs materials like underfill, gap-fill, surface chemistry, or TSV consumables.
KLIC should remain in the HBM stack-flow universe as a thermocompression bonding equipment candidate; key survival test is whether TCB orders are HBM/AI-specific and material to revenue.
CAMT is a strong underfollowed HBM yield-management candidate because official materials link it to advanced-packaging inspection/metrology and a leading HBM manufacturer order.
FORM belongs in the HBM test/probe-card subnode because HBM known-good-die and stack-die testing can become a hidden yield chokepoint.
ACMR has plausible but not yet proven HBM stack-flow exposure through wafer-level advanced-packaging process tools; needs direct HBM/TSV/customer evidence before promotion from speculative_shadow.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the US-listed universe for the HBM stack and advanced-packaging process-tool node. The cleanest US-listed direct exposures found in this pass are inspection/metrology and test/probe-card suppliers rather than HBM memory producers. CAMT, FORM, and ONTO belong in the underfollowed lane because their products touch HBM yield, inspection, metrology, or known-good-die validation. AMKR is included as a reference/direct OSAT capacity anchor for advanced packaging, but its exposure is broader and less pure to the HBM stack flow than process-control and test-tool vendors. Expanded the US-listed universe one layer beneath HBM producers, focused on die/wafer test, thermocompression bonding, TSV/advanced-packaging wet process, and inspection/metrology yield management. The cleanest US-listed underfollowed candidates found in this pass are Kulicke & Soffa, FormFactor, Camtek, and Onto Innovation. These are not trading recommendations; they are Layer 1B research candidates requiring revenue-exposure verification, customer/order checks, and valuation/expectations checks in later layers. Expanded the US-listed universe for the HBM stack and advanced-packaging process-tool node. The reference lane anchors demand with Micron as a US-listed HBM producer. The underfollowed lane prioritizes process-control, probe-card, and bonding/tooling suppliers whose exposure sits beneath HBM producers: Onto Innovation for HBM inspection and 3D bump metrology, FormFactor for HBM probe-card testing, and Kulicke & Soffa for thermocompression / advanced memory bonding systems.
